svg.title: What a random forest does
svg.desc: A random forest builds many decision trees. Five small trees appear, each learning from a different random sample of the students. A new made-up student is shown to each tree and each tree votes on whether the student will finish the term. Four trees say yes and one says no, and the most common vote is the forest's answer. A forest is usually more accurate than one tree, but it cannot be read as a single set of rules.

text.tspan: Each tree votes on a new student
Each tree learns from a different random sample.
Each tree votes on a new student.
The most common vote is the forest's answer.
Usually more accurate than one tree, but harder to read.
